Members that are residuals

Source: R/scale-class.R
scale_residuals.Rd

A residual carries a real value but is not a destination for allocation: non-regionalized GDP, taxes that belong to no industry, an "n.e.c." bucket. It aggregates upward like any other member – that is the point, it is what makes the parent total reconcile – but recast_scale() never splits a coarse figure INTO one.

Usage

scale_residuals(x, frame = NULL)

Arguments

x

A NestedScale.

frame

A single frame name for just that frame's residuals, or NULL for the whole named list.

Value

A character vector of member codes, or the named list over frames. Empty when the scale declares none.

Details

Declare them when building the scale, per frame, because codes are not unique across frames: scale_from_leaftable(..., residuals = list(item = "DE_XR")).

Examples

s <- scale_example()
scale_residuals(s) # none declared
#> list()

lf <- scale_leaftable(s)
r <- scale_from_leaftable(
  lf,
  frames = scale_frames(s), leaf = "item",
  weights = scale_weights(s), name = "with_residual",
  residuals = list(item = "OTH")
)
scale_residuals(r, "item")
#> [1] "OTH"
